paper.title: Do Transitional Justice Museums Persuade Visitors? Evidence from a Field Experiment

engine: Claude Code (Claude Agent SDK) - Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) via Anthropic

claims.claim: After visiting the museum, satisfaction with the current government increases (b = 0.15, p = .04).
Satisfaction with democracy increases following a museum visit (b = 0.14, p = .03).
Satisfaction with democracy increases particularly among those on the left (b = 0.16, p = .10).
Individuals increase their trust in the church (b = .18, p = .01).
Support for a military government drops 11% after visiting.
Those treated on the right decrease their acceptance of a military government by 17%.
The right-left gap in acceptance of a military government is reduced from 0.43 to 0.34 after visiting the museum.
The partisan divide in satisfaction with democracy is reduced from 0.26 to 0.12 after treatment.
Subjects are less likely to believe that dwelling on the past prevents progress (b = -0.32, p = .03).
Greater support for victim compensation (b = 0.19, p = .00).
Greater support for a public apology from the military (b = 0.18, p = .09).
Visitors are more likely to say perpetrators should be pardoned (b = 0.22, p = .02).
Only 13.14% (n = 18) indicated that the information in the museum was new to them.
After one week, treated participants are still more likely to support pardoning (b = 0.20, p = .16).
126 control participants showed up; 143 treatment participants showed up, 5 of whom did not visit (CACE).
Final follow-up round sample size n = 131.
Figures 1-4 (coefficient plots) are produced by the shipped code.

findings.description: The shipped main-text script BPV_museums_maintext.R stops at Figure 2 (line 224) with "replacement has 25 rows, data has 24": the label loop `for (i in 22:34)` writes past the 24-row data frame. Figures 2-4 and all later estimates are not produced as shipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the loop bound to 22:24 (applied in working/ as a lossless edit; no estimate, SE or p-value changes).

findings.description: C14: the text attributes b = 0.20, p = .16 to the one-week follow-up. The one-week (wave 1) estimate recomputes to b = 0.308, p = .004 (n = 222); b = 0.20, p = .16 equals the 24-week (wave 3) estimate (b = 0.205, p = .164, n = 129). Published Figure 4B also shows a week-1 point near 0.31 and a week-24 point near 0.20, so the code reproduces the figure and the text label does not match it. P2 because it is a secondary (durability) result and the figure reproduces.
findings.evidence: results/estimates.csv rows pardoned_f1, pardoned_f3; figures/figure4_durability.pdf vs published p. 507.
findings.suggested_fix: Authors could state which wave the in-text durability statistic refers to.

findings.description: C13: n = 18 recurs, but 13.14% does not: 18/135 non-missing treated answers = 13.33%, 18/138 treated = 13.04%. 13.14% equals 18/137; 137 is the non-missing count of several other post-visit items among treated (e.g. justice_advance), so the percentage may use another item's denominator; this could not be confirmed.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the denominator used for the 13.14% figure.

findings.description: Reported p-values equal the heteroscedasticity-consistent p-value divided by itt.d (0.965): the code divides the whole coeftest row (estimate, SE, t and p) by itt.d. With the division, C3 (.096 -> .10) and C11 (.088 -> .09) match the text; without it they would read .09 and .08. Recorded as computed; not a judgement on the method.
findings.evidence: est.ate() and est.ate.np() in BPV_museums_maintext.R; raw p = reported p x 0.965.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the methods how p-values for the CACE are obtained.

findings.description: Two-decimal reporting is not uniform: C10 (b = 0.198 reported 0.19; p = .009 reported .00) and C7 (0.436 reported 0.43) match truncation; C1 p = .0350 is reported as .04 (neither rounding nor truncation gives .04). Differences are in the last digit only.
findings.suggested_fix: Report values rounded consistently, or with three decimals for p.

findings.description: No README, software versions or run instructions are shipped; Figure 4 is drawn with base graphics to the default device and never saved by the script; the Figure 1 label loop `for (i in 13:25)` overruns into later groups (harmless, later loops overwrite the labels).
findings.suggested_fix: Ship a README with R and package versions and save Figure 4 explicitly.

limitations: Pilot run: the bundle is not yet published; github_url points to the ReproCrowd project repository, not to a repository holding this bundle.
No nanopublications were minted (artifacts.chain_uris is empty); see nanopubs/PUBLISHED.md.
The appendix script ran unmodified to exit 0, but appendix tables A1-A22 were not compared with the online appendix.
C7 and C8 use the certifier's operationalisation of the right-left gap (difference in means among treated, pre vs post); the paper does not state the computation.
Run on one platform (macOS arm64); linux-64 is solved in pixi.lock but was not executed.
The rule pack's verify_quote / resolve_doi / wikidata_lookup tools were not available; claims were transcribed from pdftotext output of the paper PDF and checked by reading.
